newsitem.title: FRANCE: Car bomb kills four, wounds 30 in Algiers - radio.
newsitem.headline: Car bomb kills four, wounds 30 in Algiers - radio.

text.p: A car bomb exploded on Monday in Algiers, killing four people and wounding 30, said the Algerian state-run radio quoting a security services statement.

The blast in Kouba, a Moslem guerrilla stronghold in the Algerian capital, came after a wave of bombings and massacres in Algiers and neighbouring towns in January and early February in which more than 300 people were killed.
Residents, speaking by telephone from Algiers, said two other car bombs exploded on Monday afternoon in Jolie Vue and Anasser, two districts near Kouba, killing at least seven people.
The residents' reports could not be immediately confirmed by official and diplomatic sources in Algiers.
The reported blasts came as the authorities were calling on people to register for June 5 parliamentary elections from which radical Islamists are barred from fielding candidates.

They followed the security forces unleashing huge search operations which killed more than 50 rebels in Algiers and the western province of Relizane on Saturday, according to residents and Algerian newspapers.
The Algerian authorities blame Moslem guerrillas for the violence, including bombings and massacres of civilians in remote villages.

About 60,000 people have died in Algeria's conflict pitting Moslem guerrillas against government forces since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a huge lead.
